newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down in slow trade on Tuesday on profit-taking by retail investors following overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,890 yuan ($2,879) per tonne, losing 70 yuan. It opened at 23,930 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,940 and a low of 23,850 yuan.
April fell 50 to 23,500, May 80 to 23,600, June 90 to 23,830, August 80 to 23,860 and September 200 to 23,800.
Combined volume fell sharply to 22,940 tonnes from 44,100.
Copper opened slightly lower on LME losses and moved in a narrow range for most of the session with wary retail investors liquidating their long positions, traders said.
"Long liquidation from retail investors was the major factor behind today's fall while most investors remained on the sidelines with market direction unclear," one trader said.
Traders said the LME would be a major factor influencing Shanghai copper in the abesence of domestic market-moving news in the next few days.
"Shanghai copper will move in a narrow range following LME gains or losses in the short term," a second trader said.
